16599-school-church-and-home-games.title: School Church And Home Games
16599-school-church-and-home-games.creator: Unknown
16599-school-church-and-home-games.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. One pupil is designated to play the role of cat, another that of mouse. The mouse can escape the cat by sitting in the seat with some other pupil. Thereupon that pupil becomes mouse. Should the cat tag a mouse before it sits in a seat, the mouse becomes cat and the cat becomes mouse, and the latter must get into a seat to avoid being tagged.

42014-meg-of-mystery-mountain.title: Meg Of Mystery Mountain
42014-meg-of-mystery-mountain.creator: Grace May North
42014-meg-of-mystery-mountain.description: A book by Grace May North. Marion had evidently thought of the same thing, for she laughingly ran up the gang plank, her arms filled with candy boxes, boquets and magazines, gifts of her admiring friends. Depositing these on a chair, she leaned over the rail to call: "Good-bye, girls! Of course I'll write to you, Sally, reams and reams; a sort of a round-robin letter to be sent to the whole crowd.

arxiv-2001-10474.title: Coagent Networks Revisited
arxiv-2001-10474.creator: Modjtaba Shokrian Zini, Mohammad Pedramfar, Matthew Riemer, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Miao Liu
arxiv-2001-10474.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Modjtaba Shokrian Zini, Mohammad Pedramfar, Matthew Riemer, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Miao Liu. Coagent networks formalize the concept of arbitrary networks of stochastic agents that collaborate to take actions in a reinforcement learning environment. Prominent examples of coagent networks in action include approaches to hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL), such as those using options, which attempt to address the exploration exploitation trade-off by introducing abstract actions at different levels by sequencing multiple stochastic networks within the HRL agents.

arxiv-2011-06588.title: The classical double copy in curved spacetimes: Perturbative Yang-Mills from the bi-adjoint scalar
arxiv-2011-06588.creator: Siddharth G. Prabhu
arxiv-2011-06588.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Siddharth G. Prabhu. We formulate a version of the double copy for classical fields in curved spacetimes. We provide a correspondence between perturbative solutions to the bi-adjoint scalar equations and those of the Yang-Mills equations in position space. At the linear level, we show that there exists a map between these solutions for maximally symmetric spacetime backgrounds, that provides every Yang-Mills solution by the action of an appropriate differential operator on a bi-adjoint scalar solution.

arxiv-2202-11821.title: Physics-informed neural networks for inverse problems in supersonic flows Journal: Journal
arxiv-2202-11821.creator: Ameya D. Jagtap 1,† , Zhiping Mao 2,† , Nikolaus Adams 3 , and George Em Karniadakis 1
arxiv-2202-11821.description: Abstract Accurate solutions to inverse supersonic compressible flow problems are often required for designing specialized aerospace vehicles. In particular, we consider the problem where we have data available for density gradients from Schlieren photography as well as data at the inflow and part of wall boundaries.

arxiv-2305-19197.title: Interpreting dark matter solution for B − L B-L gauge symmetry
arxiv-2305-19197.creator: Phung Van Dong
arxiv-2305-19197.description: Abstract It is shown that the solution for B − L B-L gauge symmetry with B − L = − 4 , − 4 , + 5 B-L=-4,-4,+5 assigned for three right-handed neutrinos respectively, reveals a novel scotogenic mechanism with implied matter parity for neutrino mass generation and dark matter stability. Additionally, the world with two-component dark matter is hinted.

arxiv-2405-14733.title: Space-time statistics of 2D soliton gas in shallow water studied by stereoscopic surface mapping
arxiv-2405-14733.creator: T. Leduque, E. Barthélemy, H. Michallet, J. Sommeria, N. Mordant
arxiv-2405-14733.description: Abstract We describe laboratory experiments in a 2D wave tank that aim at building up and monitor 2D shallow water soliton gas. The water surface elevation is obtained over a large ( ∼ 100 ​ m 2 \sim 100\,\text{m}^{2} ) domain, with centimetre-resolution, by stereoscopic vision using two cameras.

arxiv-2408-15313.title: Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization: Balancing Safety-Helpfulness in Language Models
arxiv-2408-15313.creator: Wenxuan Zhang, Philip H.S. Torr, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Adel Bibi
arxiv-2408-15313.description: Abstract Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on human preferences, typically through reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), has proven successful in enhancing their capabilities. However, ensuring the safety of LLMs during fine-tuning remains a critical concern, and mitigating the potential conflicts in safety and helpfulness is costly in RLHF.

arxiv-2409-05454.title: Probing strangeness with event topology classifiers in pp collisions at energies available at the CERN Large Hadron Collider with the rope hadronization mechanism in PYTHIA
arxiv-2409-05454.creator: Suraj Prasad 1, Bhagyarathi Sahoo 1, Sushanta Tripathy 2, Neelkamal Mallick 1, Raghunath Sahoo 1
arxiv-2409-05454.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Suraj Prasad 1, Bhagyarathi Sahoo 1, Sushanta Tripathy 2, Neelkamal Mallick 1, Raghunath Sahoo 1. In relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the formation of a deconfined and thermalized state of partons, known as quark-gluon plasma (QGP), leads to enhanced production of strange hadrons in contrast to proton-proton (pp) collisions, which are taken as baseline. This observation is known as strangeness enhancement in heavy-ion collisions and is considered one of the important signatures that can signify the formation of QGP.

arxiv-2505-13337.title: Neural-Enhanced Rate Adaptation and Computation Distribution for Emerging mmWave Multi-User 3D Video Streaming Systems
arxiv-2505-13337.creator: Babak Badnava 1 , Jacob Chakareski 2 , Morteza Hashemi 1
arxiv-2505-13337.description: Abstract We investigate multitask edge-user communication-computation resource allocation for 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} video streaming in an edge-computing enabled millimeter wave (mmWave) multi-user virtual reality system. To balance the communication-computation trade-offs that arise herein, we formulate a video quality maximization problem that integrates interdependent multitask/multi-user action spaces and rebuffering time/quality variation constraints.

pmc-10540381.title: A case report and literature review on a rare subtype of triple-negative breast cancer in children
pmc-10540381.creator: Lexiang Shi, Yinan Zhang, Jingcheng Wu, Jinping Li, Junzhao Zhu, Youbo Xu, Nie Li, Qin Li, Wanli Zhang
pmc-10540381.description: BackgroundTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a type of breast tumor with a poor prognosis because it lacks or expresses low levels of estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER-2). TNBC is more common in middle-aged and older women, and cases of TNBC in children are rarely reported.

pmc-10605660.title: A Simple Exercise Program for Patients With End-Stage Kidney Disease to Improve Strength and Quality of Life: Clinical Research Protocol
pmc-10605660.creator: Rita S. Suri, Louise Moist, Charmaine Lok, Catherine M. Clase, Jennifer Harris, Robert D. Reid, Tim Ramsay, Deborah Zimmerman
pmc-10605660.description: Background:Most patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) appreciate the importance of exercise and would like to increase their physical activity; however, they report a few key barriers, including (1) lack of physician advice to do so, (2) lack of safe and convenient programs (ie, appropriate for home or neighborhood), and (3) cost.

pmc-11445010.title: Eating disorder risk assessment and sociocultural attitudes toward body image among Polish and Turkish professional female football players
pmc-11445010.creator: Wiktoria Staśkiewicz-Bartecka, Samet Aktaş, Grzegorz Zydek, Marek Kardas, Martyna Kałuża, Małgorzata Magdalena Michalczyk
pmc-11445010.description: hes, and sports systems, to achieve and maintain a particular body shape for optimal performance and to meet esthetic ideals (2–5). pmc-11641232.title: Efficacy and Safety of Virtual Reality-Based Versus Traditional Emotion-to-Emotion Therapy for Treatment of Hwa-Byung: A Protocol for a Single-Center, Randomized, Assessor-Blind, Parallel-Group Clinical Trial
pmc-11641232.creator: Hye Jeong Kook, Dong Hoon Kang, Yang Chun Park, Nam Kwen Kim, Hyung Won Kang, In Chul Jung, Roberto Pedone
pmc-11641232.description: Background: Hwa-Byung is a culturally bound syndrome prevalent in Korea, characterized by intense emotional distress and physical symptoms related to suppressed anger. Patients frequently report experiencing chest tightness, heat sensations, and globus pharyngeus (the sensation of a lump in the throat).

pmc-11714291.title: Bone morphogenetic protein levels relate to osteoarthritis and neurobehavioral outcomes in cognitively unimpaired older adults
pmc-11714291.creator: Valentina E. Diaz, Emily W. Paolillo, Coty Chen, Anna M. VandeBunte, Claire J. Cadwallader, Charles A. Schurman, Birgit Schiling, Bruce L. Miller, Joel H. Kramer, Kaitlin B. Casaletto, Rowan Saloner
pmc-11714291.description: BackgroundOsteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disorder of bone aging and risk factor for cognitive decline. Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) are growth factor proteins that regulate skeletal and neural development, and circulating BMPs may mediate molecular cross‐talk between bone and brain. The present study examined plasma BMP levels in relation to OA and neurobehavioral outcomes in cognitively unimpaired (CU) older adults.

pmc-12591613.title: Impact of Daily Maximum Temperature on Emergency Department Arrivals and Acuity Levels
pmc-12591613.creator: Catharina Giudice, Nicholas J Arisco, Zilin Lu, Bryan Stenson, Caleb Dresser
pmc-12591613.description: IntroductionHeatwaves are becoming more frequent and severe globally. Heat is associated with increases in emergency department (ED) volumes and higher morbidity for a range of chronic conditions. We describe how temperature impacts ED arrivals at different acuity levels.MethodsWe obtained time-series records for daily ED arrivals stratified by Emergency Severity Index (ESI) from 2010 – 2019 from hospital records.

pmc-12643350.title: Hypercrosslinked Polymers for Volatile and Very Volatile Organic Compound Capture Beyond Commercial Benchmarks
pmc-12643350.creator: Paul Schweng, Elias Rippatha, Clemens Schwarzinger, Robert T Woodward
pmc-12643350.description: The effective capture of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and very volatile organic compounds (VVOCs) is crucial for controlling indoor air quality, environmental monitoring, and emission regulation. However, effective VVOC adsorption remains challenging due to their low boiling points, high vapour pressures, and the susceptibility of many adsorbents to competitive water sorption.

pmc-12741056.title: Kidney bean detection in complex agricultural scenarios based on the kidneyB-YOLO model
pmc-12741056.creator: Jianjia Qi, Chunxiang Liu, Hongxia Chu
pmc-12741056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThis study addresses the problem of detecting multiple targets and occluded kidney beans in the complex agricultural scenarios under the open-field trellis cultivation.MethodsA target detection model based on kidneyB-YOLO is proposed. The model integrated the dynamic convolution module, the Deformable Attention Transformer (DAT) attention mechanism, the feature fusion detection head improved Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) detection method, and the Focaler-SIoU loss function. The dynamic convolution module adaptively adjusted parameters based on the input.

pmc-12986468.title: Tubular Epithelia-Specific Deletion of MCP-1 Does Not Afford Protection Against Adriamycin-Induced Kidney Injury
pmc-12986468.creator: Corry D. Bondi, Hannah L. Hartman, Josie L. Gilbert, Joy A. Stewart, Dennis R. Clayton, Roderick J. Tan
pmc-12986468.description: The increasing global burden of chronic kidney disease (CKD) magnifies an urgent need to find treatable targets. Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1/CCL2) is a chemokine secreted by kidney tubular epithelia in response to a variety of stimuli. To better understand the effects of tubular MCP-1 in response to kidney injury, we generated tubular epithelia-specific MCP-1 knockout mice (KO; Pax8-Mcp-1fl/fl).

pmc-13218463.title: Driving factors in pediatric emergency department use: an ecological retrospective study
pmc-13218463.creator: Denis Mongin, Hervé Spechbach, Joachim Marti, Frederic Ehrler, Johan N. Siebert, Afagh Hassanzadeh Rad, Ilse Bloom, Helga Naburi, Helga Naburi
pmc-13218463.description: BackgroundPediatric emergency departments (PEDs) often face high volumes of low-acuity visits, reflecting gaps in primary care access and socio-economic disparities. We investigated how neighborhood socio-economic vulnerability, pediatrician availability, and proximity to the PED jointly influence PED utilization in Geneva, Switzerland.

pmc-13240264.title: Network Pharmacology and Integrated Experimental Evidence Demonstrate That Ophiopogonin D Suppresses Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression via the UCK2–SLC7A11 Axis
pmc-13240264.creator: Yuxia Hao, Haris Muhammad, Yushi Wang, Yan Wang, Lu Cui, Jiajia Quan, Bing Xie, Xi Li
pmc-13240264.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatment faces significant challenges, including high toxicity and drug resistance. Ophiopogonin D, the active compound derived from the medicinal food material Ophiopogon japonicus (Mai Dong), has demonstrated potential anti‐cancer properties. However, its specific mechanism in combating HCC remains unclear.

pmc-13263818.title: When the kidney is at risk: anaesthetic technique as one piece of a larger puzzle
pmc-13263818.creator: Carlo Andrea Bravi, Alberto Martini
pmc-13263818.description: ongly associated with prolonged hospital stay, progression to chronic kidney disease (2) and increased mortality (3). Identifying potentially modifiable intra-operative factors, including the choice of anaesthetic, is therefore of major relevance to anaesthetists and perioperative physicians (4,5). The authors should be commended for conducting a rigorously designed randomised controlled trial in a surgical population at intrinsically high renal risk.

pmc-13300937.title: DHA-Derived Lipid Mediators Attenuate Osteoarthritis by Resolving Inflammation and Protecting Cartilage in Association with the SIRT1 Signaling Pathway
pmc-13300937.creator: Yan Su, Soon Kyu Kwon, Hack Sun Choi, Yunjon Han, Jung-Hee Park, Jong Hyun Choi, Jeong-Woo Seo
pmc-13300937.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by persistent low-grade inflammation and progressive cartilage destruction. Macrophage-driven inflammatory responses contribute to extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and accelerate disease progression. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of a DHA-derived lipid mediator mixture (LM), generated via soybean lipoxygenase and composed of 17S-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid, resolvin D5, and protectin DX (3:47:50), in regulating macrophage–chondrocyte crosstalk and OA progression. LM significantly reduced IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α production in lipopolysaccharide-induced THP-1 macrophages.

pmc-13339924.title: Sugar restriction during the first 1000 days after conception and its association with decreased risk of anxiety and depression
pmc-13339924.creator: Xiuping Dou, Yang Su, Yao Huang, Man He, Bingying Zhang, Xuejin Li, Hualiang Lin, Yin Yang
pmc-13339924.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDepression and anxiety pose a major challenge to global public mental health, and early life exposures are known to exert substantial long‐term effects. However, evidence on the long‐term effect of sugar restriction during the first 1000 days after conception on mental health remains limited, and it is still unclear whether such restriction reduces the subsequent risk of anxiety and depression in later life.AimsTo examine whether sugar restriction during the first 1000 days after conception is associated with a reduced risk of anxiety

pmc-13364193.title: Food as Medicine: Effects of a Culinary Medicine Food-Demonstration on Medical Students’ Nutrition Knowledge, Confidence, and Satisfaction: An Exploratory Pilot Non-Randomized Pre-Post Intervention Study
pmc-13364193.creator: Niayesh Mardmomen, Cyrus Fatemi, Olivia K. Smith, Michael Roberts, Farzaneh Daghigh
pmc-13364193.description: Background: Diet plays a central role in the development of chronic diseases, making nutrition-focused interventions a powerful tool for improving population health. However, substantial gaps in nutrition education persist in the U.S. medical education, and medical students frequently report receiving limited nutrition training despite its importance in patient care.

pmc-13416041.title: Phytohormones and Shoot Branching: A Mini-Review of Molecular Regulatory Networks and Mechanisms
pmc-13416041.creator: Xingxing Zhang, Miao Chai, Yijia Wu, Jialei Tang, Cong Yin, Lu Zhang, Shuai Gao
pmc-13416041.description: As a crucial component of plant architecture, shoot branching significantly enhances photosynthetic efficiency and optimizes the source-sink allocation of photosynthetic products, which directly impacts crop productivity. The formation of lateral branches is co-regulated by various internal and external factors, including genetic factors, phytohormones, metabolic, and environmental factors.
